newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed in selective trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed in selective trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed with a positive bias on Monday in selective trading, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 0.11 percent, or 0.29 points, to 259.55 on all-share turnover of 150 million shekels against 175 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.10 percent higher at 268.38.

"Trading continues to be mixed and selective. For the second consecutive day trading opened with excess supply (in the leader) but (prices) closed with a moderate rise. This shows how strong the market is," said Idan Azoulay of Impact Union Portfolio Management.

"Activity continues to be brisk and the market looks good. Trading was very selective today. I believe the market will continue to rise, but it will be more selective," said a trader at Evergreen Capital Markets.
"A correction has to come. The only question is when it will happen and how strong it will be," Azoulay added. "In the near term the market is expected to be more selective."
"We are all waiting for the offering of Israel Discount Bank next week. A successful offer will give the market a push and the positive momentum will continue," the Evergreen trader said.

The Israeli government will be offering 17 percent of the bank, Israel's third largest, in a package of shares and warrants worth approximately 630 million shekels at the bank's current market capitalisation.
Market sources said the offer would be priced at a slight discount to the market price.
On Monday Discount Bank lost 2.0 percent to 390 agorot.

Dead Sea Works, the main gainer on the Maof, rose 3.0 percent to 1,053 agorot. Sahar Securities and Investments said in report released on Sunday rated the company a "buy" but said it carries a high degree of risk.

The most active share was Poalim Capital Markets and Investments, which rose 1.0 percent to 14,271 on volume of 11.3 million shekels. Traders said the share rose on purchasing by major shareholders in the company.
Other active shares include Clal Israel, which fell 1.0 percent to 110 agorot on turnover of 7.9 million shekels, and Koor Industries, which gained 0.75 percent to 36,113 agorot.
